text:
sara: FYI support ticket from Acme — they reported a sudden p95 jump after today's runtime rollout. Baseline p95 ~180ms, now ~620ms for their traffic. They started seeing it at ~14:04 UTC.
marco: ack. which release did we push to their cohort?
sara: rollout tagged runtime/v2.3.1, canary flagged green at 13:50. traffic was ramped to 20% at 14:00.
jess: @sara can you paste the customer request sample + route? want to repro locally.
sara: request example: `POST /v1/generate` body: `{prompt: "short summary", max_tokens: 128}` header x-customer-id: acme-corp. Route: model=reverb-7b, tenant=acme-prod, seq_len=512.
lee: quick check — dashboards show a cohort-level p95 spike aligned with that ramp. p50 unchanged. p99 also up but noisier. looks like tail, not throughput saturation.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout runtime/v2.3.1 -> 20% traffic @ 14:00 UTC (commit a1b2c3d).
marco: hypothesis: changed kernel selector + quant scheduling in v2.3.1. new selector prefers fused-matmul kernel that regresses some sequence-length/temperature combos. also we shipped a scheduler change that increases batch window under low concurrency.
jess: can we shadow traffic to the previous runtime and compare latencies? i can spin a traffic-shadow job.
sara: I've already captured traces and attached flame graph link: https://dash.redwood.com/trace/1714500000/acme-p95-spike (shortlink)
lee: logs show increased time in `kv_cache_lookup` and `batch_wait_ms` for the slow traces. sample log: ```
[14:03:12.123] req=abcd token=... stage=kv_cache_lookup dt=42ms
[14:03:12.165] req=abcd stage=batch_wait dt=210ms
[14:03:12.376] req=abcd stage=kernel_exec dt=320ms
```
marco: interesting — batch_wait 210ms suggests our batching heuristics waited for more tokens than before. that can blow p95 when bursty traffic hits a new scheduler.
jess: running a canary-shadow compare now: routing 5% traffic to runtime/v2.2.9 (prod) and 5% to v2.3.1 with same requests. will report diff.
sara: customer is hitting timeouts; suggested short-term mitigation to them: reduce max_concurrency=1 and set `prefer_variant=v2.2.9` on their account until we triage. they asked for ETA.
marco: immediate mitigation from our side: 1) toggle scheduler flag `burst_aggregation_enabled=false` for v2.3 cohort (hot-config) 2) fallback kernel selector to 'legacy' for reverb-7b on v2.3 (hotpatch). both low-risk.
lee: steps to toggle: 
```
# disable burst aggregation
rdctl runtime-config set v2.3.1 --key scheduler.burst_aggregation_enabled --value false --cohort acme-prod
# fallback kernel
rdctl kernel-selector set reverb-7b --policy legacy --runtime v2.3.1
```
marco: also recommend enabling prefix/KV warmup for acme-prod: run their recent prompts through warmup queue to populate caches.
ops-bot: perf-diff job queued: compare p95(v2.2.9) vs p95(v2.3.1) on acme-synth load. job id 1714500102.
jess: perf-diff results (quick): p50 ~ same, p95 v2.2.9=185ms, v2.3.1=610ms, breakdown: batch_wait + kernel_exec delta ~+350ms.
sara: customer agreed to temporary prefer_variant while we patch. they asked for root cause and next steps.
marco: root cause hypothesis: scheduler change reduced immediate dispatch frequency -> longer batch windows under small bursts -> inflated batch_wait -> some kernels also slower for mid-length sequences. plan: revert scheduler heuristic for small tenants, add threshold on batch window when seq_len>256, and ship a kernel micro-optimization.
lee: triage plan: 1) hot-config toggle (execute now) 2) shadow diff confirm 3) bisect recent commits between 2.2.9 and 2.3.1 focusing on scheduler and kernel selector diffs 4) run more cohort synths across temp/seq_len ranges 5) patch and roll canary 6) notify customer with timeline.
jess: I'm on bisect. first commit to check: `scheduler: adjust_batch_wait_threshold` (commit d4e5f6). repro script I'm using: 
```
python tools/synth_load.py --tenant acme-prod --model reverb-7b --seq 512 --qps 8 --template samples/acme_prompts.json
```
marco: if bisect confirms scheduler param, we can ship a small delta to tune window to <= 30ms for low qps.
sara: timeline to customer: temp prefer_variant applied now, expect improved p95 in ~5 minutes. we'll follow up with RCA in 6-8 hours. they want call if not resolved.
ops-bot: config change applied: scheduler.burst_aggregation_enabled=false for cohort acme-prod on v2.3.1 (change id cfg-1714500200).
lee: monitoring shows p95 dropping from 620ms -> 210ms within 3 minutes after config flip. p99 improved too.
jess: bisect result: culprit commit is d4e5f6 (scheduler threshold change) + combined with kernel default change ksel-88 that makes worst case kernel exec slower. both together amplified tail.
marco: mitigation: keep hot-config disable and patch kernel micro-opt. plan to revert ksel-88 for reverb-7b in next canary and re-enable tuned scheduler after tests.
sara: I'll update customer: issue mitigated by preferring v2.2.9 and hot-config toggle, full RCA/patch ETA 4 hours.
marco: add postmortem checklist: include perf histograms, bisect steps, exact synth workload, deploy ids, and a remediation playbook for similar scheduler regressions.
sara: thanks all — leaving thread open for the patch rollout notes. :white_check_mark:
